hourly.summary: United fans are wallowing in the grim reality of the post-Fergie era — thoroughly 'brothered' by their noisy neighbors, admitting the 'stain' of City's dominance will linger even if the Abu Dhabi project collapses. The mood is equal parts embarrassing, depressing, and paranoid, with one poster conceding City 'Clasm-ed us pretty darn good' while United heaped 'shit on our own plate.' Only the ticket touts and nostalgia merchants (1968 ticket stubs, Brobbey transfer gossip) offer brief respite from the existential dread.

daily.summary: The day began with apprehension over ownership and debt, briefly lifted by Zirkzee's recall, then exploded into peak schadenfreude when City's charges dominated the afternoon narrative. By evening, the mood settled into a familiar cynicism — United fans laughing at their neighbours while roasting their own club's £1.15bn debt and Glazer ownership in the same breath.

weekly.summary: Manchester United fan sentiment remained locked in a profound, unrelenting crisis throughout the week, with daily scores clustered at 2-3/10 and no meaningful improvement. The mood deepened from post-derby outrage and Carabao Cup collapse into a settled, existential conviction that the club is structurally broken — encompassing ownership (INEOS/Glazers), management (Carrick), recruitment, identity, and physical conditioning. A fleeting shift to 'resigned' despair mid-week only underscored the fatigue of repeated cycles, before sentiment plunged back to 'catastrophic' and 'crisis' lows.
